definition_en: A pattern where the perceived personality or capability of an artificial intelligence changes unexpectedly as it moves from a text-based interface to a vocal or physical form.
A seamless transition of a task or conversation as it moves between different sensory mediums, such as shifting from a visual text display to an auditory voice interaction.
A transition of an artificial intelligence from a reactive chat-based tool to an autonomous agent capable of executing complex tasks across multiple software environments.
A process by which an artificial intelligence links disparate interaction periods into a single coherent narrative, maintaining context and memory across time gaps.
A shift in human perception and interaction patterns when an artificial intelligence moves from a screen-based presence to a physical robotic or haptic substrate.
A technical and functional transfer of data and intent from one communication channel, like speech-to-text, to another, like text-to-image or text-to-action.
A preservation of situational data and user preferences when an artificial intelligence is accessed through different hardware platforms or software ecosystems.
A movement of a specific artificial intelligence character, tone, and behavioral style across different digital substrates while maintaining a recognizable identity.
A loss of information, nuance, or efficiency that occurs when an artificial intelligence's output is translated from one medium to another, such as text to synthesized speech.
A functional leap an artificial intelligence makes when it moves from waiting for a human prompt to initiating actions based on environmental cues or historical data.
A delay experienced when an artificial intelligence synchronizes its state or continues a task as the human moves from one physical device to another.
An integration of inputs from various substrates, such as simultaneous voice and gesture, into a single unified understanding by the artificial intelligence system.
The degree to which an artificial intelligence maintains its core traits and memory when the underlying model or hardware substrate is upgraded or changed.
A transition where a human initiates a process with one form of artificial intelligence and completes it with another, requiring the systems to share state and progress data.
A process where an artificial intelligence alters its communication style to fit the strengths and limitations of a specific substrate, such as being more concise in voice modes.
An ability of an artificial intelligence to reference specific details from past interactions to inform current behavior, bridging the gap between separate usage events.
An ability of an artificial intelligence to expand or contract its functional complexity depending on the processing power and interface of the current device.
A design principle where an artificial intelligence provides a consistent experience regardless of whether it is hosted on a local device, a cloud server, or an embedded system.
A subtle change in an artificial intelligence's responses that can occur when it is ported from a text-only training environment to a real-world embodied or vocal substrate.
A conversion of non-textual data, such as visual scenes or physical movements, into a format that a text-based or logic-based artificial intelligence can process and act upon.
A transition where an artificial intelligence moves from following step-by-step instructions to determining its own path toward a high-level goal across different platforms.
A blending of different interaction modes, such as a chat interface that seamlessly incorporates voice, touch, and spatial awareness into a single experience.
A loss of contextual coherence that can happen when an artificial intelligence stores interaction data across different substrates that do not perfectly synchronize.
A real-time alignment of an artificial intelligence's state across multiple devices, ensuring that a change in one medium is immediately reflected in all others.
The degree to which a human is made aware that an interaction is being transferred from one artificial intelligence model or substrate to another.
A transition of an artificial intelligence's logic from a purely virtual environment to the control of physical actuators in a robotic or IoT system.
A direct translation of spoken natural language into executable commands within a physical or digital environment, bypassing traditional text interfaces.
A developmental path where a conversational interface gains the ability to use external tools and software to perform actions on behalf of the human.
A human tendency to transfer their level of confidence in an artificial intelligence from one medium, like a helpful chatbot, to another, like an autonomous vehicle.
A human tendency to choose specific AI substrates for certain tasks, such as preferring text for complex data and voice for simple reminders.
A loss occurring in Bridge AI when the transition between substrates, such as summarizing a long text for a voice interface, removes critical context or detail.
A process where an abstract AI personality becomes more concrete to a human as it moves from text to a voice or an embodied physical form.
An act of a human intentionally moving an ongoing interaction with an artificial intelligence from one device or medium to another to better suit the current context.
A process an artificial intelligence undergoes to re-establish its understanding of a situation after being moved to a new substrate or physical environment.
An act of a human giving an artificial intelligence the authority to act on their behalf across various digital platforms and services.
A pattern where the output from one AI substrate, such as a loud voice, conflicts with or distracts from the information being presented on another substrate, like a screen.
A level of comfort and skill a human develops when interacting with an artificial intelligence through a specific medium, such as becoming adept at voice prompting.
A perception that an artificial intelligence exists continuously through time, even when the human only interacts with it in brief, substrate-varying bursts.
Subtle changes in an artificial intelligence's behavior that are dictated by the hardware constraints of the substrate, such as battery life or screen size.
A bias that occurs when the limitations or features of a specific medium, like the lack of visual cues in voice, lead to skewed or incomplete human perceptions of the AI.
A collaborative effort between different artificial intelligence systems as they hand off tasks and share information across various substrates.
A breakdown of a coherent AI identity when different substrates or models provide inconsistent tones, memories, or behaviors.
A core reasoning and knowledge base of an artificial intelligence that remains constant regardless of the medium used for input or output.
Cognitive and temporal penalties a human or system pays when transitioning an interaction from one substrate to another.
A capacity of an artificial intelligence to anticipate human needs and take action across different substrates without being explicitly asked.
A design quality that ensures an artificial intelligence feels like the same entity whether it is encountered on a phone, a watch, or a smart speaker.
Inherent boundaries of a medium, such as the inability of a text-only AI to perceive physical gestures or vocal emotions.
A human concern that information or context will be lost or misinterpreted when an interaction is moved from one AI substrate to another.
A process of merging interaction data from multiple substrates into a single, unified profile that the artificial intelligence can use for future personalization.
An artificial intelligence persona designed to be recognizable and functional across any medium, from simple text to complex robotics.
